documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. She turns 45 next month. Says she is fine, a bit tired from summer curriculum work but nothing she wants looked into. No meds.

Screens: PHQ-2 zero.

Exam: BP and weight in her usual range. Neck without nodes. Lungs clear, heart regular without murmur. Abdomen soft, no masses. No edema. Normal affect.

Plan:
- Colorectal screening is due at 45. We talked through colonoscopy vs stool testing; she prefers the FIT. Kit handed to her, to do after her birthday.
- Lipids and CMP today.
- Mammogram order renewed for winter.
- Vaccines in October.

documents.title: Cholesterol and Chemistry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol numbers are in a good range and the chemistry panel is normal. Recheck lipids in a year or two.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stool FIT negative. Portal note sent: repeat the kit in one year.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (2024-25) left deltoid, COVID 2024-25 right deltoid. Well today. Mentions she has felt run down for a few months; advised to book a visit with the doctor for that rather than wait for her physical. She will.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since roughly June she has been dragging. Tired by midafternoon, foggy, hard to keep up with grading. Belly bloats on and off, worse later in the day. Bowels have gone irregular: a few days constipated, then loose for a day or two, back and forth. No blood, no black stool. Weight steady, eating okay. No fevers. Periods regular. Took on more at work this year and admits it has been stressful.

O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Looks tired but well. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodes. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender today, normal bowel sounds, no masses or organomegaly.

A/P: Fatigue with bloating and alternating bowel habit, ~5 months. No alarm features and FIT was negative in September. Checking CBC with diff, CMP, TSH, ferritin, celiac serology and CRP today. She would like to see GI regardless of results to sort out the bowel piece; referral placed. Will message results.

documents.title: Results From Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, everything from Monday is normal: no anemia, iron stores fine, thyroid normal, celiac test negative, inflammation marker normal, kidney and liver tests fine. Reassuring. Keep the GI appointment.

documents.title: RE: Results From Monday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good to hear. GI could fit me in December 16th, so I took it.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the GI visit from 12/16. We have no letter yet; history from Julie.

She says the gastroenterologist examined her, reviewed our November labs, and called it irritable bowel syndrome, the mixed type. Started her on polyethylene glycol powder, one capful in a drink on days she is backed up. Using it maybe twice a week. Some diet suggestions. Bloating a little better.

The bigger piece today is stress. This year she took on extra duties at school on top of her classes and has been anxious most days since early fall, lying awake running through to-do lists, waking at 4. She thinks the tiredness and the gut flares follow the bad weeks. No panic attacks. Not depressed, still enjoys weekends. No thoughts of self-harm. No substance use.

GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 6.

Exam: BP and weight stable. Appears a little tense, linear and engaged. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Assessment:
1. IBS, mixed, newly diagnosed by GI. PEG as needed added to her list per report.
2. Situational anxiety with sleep disruption, tied to the job change.

Plan: Talked through sleep habits, a fixed wind-down, caffeine before noon only. Offered a counseling referral; she would rather try on her own first and will tell me if it is not improving. No medication. Our staff will request the GI consult note. Check in by video in about three months.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called the outside GI office for the 12/16/24 consult note. They show it signed but never sent to us. Request faxed with patient's release; they said 1 to 2 weeks.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammography with tomosynthesis. Prior studies from 2022 and 2023 reviewed. Scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. Stable appearance.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Return in one year.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/16/2024
Referring: primary care
Reason: fatigue, bloating, change in bowel habit

Ms. Duffy is a 45-year-old teacher seen at the request of her primary care physician. For about half a year she has found ordinary days harder to get through: persistent tiredness, trouble thinking clearly, and bloating that comes and goes. Her stools swing between constipation and diarrhea; the amount passed is not changed. For several weeks she has felt full in the lower abdomen, a little better after a bowel movement, and needs to rest after light exertion. No meaningful weight loss, appetite largely preserved though she is not hungry first thing in the morning. She connects all of this to stress since her job responsibilities changed, and reports anxiety and poor sleep.

Past history: cesarean section at 32. No chronic illness.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with papillary thyroid cancer; father hypertension; mother osteoporosis.
Social: high school teacher, never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: Abdomen mildly distended with slight tenderness across both lower quadrants. No palpable mass, no guarding or rebound.

Data: Laboratory testing from her PCP in November is normal, including CBC, metabolic panel, TSH, ferritin, celiac serology and CRP. FIT negative 9/2024.

Impression: Irritable bowel syndrome, mixed subtype, meeting symptom criteria, with no alarm features and normal laboratory evaluation. Stress and sleep disruption likely contributing.

Recommendations:
1. Polyethylene glycol 3350, 17 g in liquid once daily as needed for constipation.
2. Soluble fiber, regular meals, trial of a reduced fermentable carbohydrate diet with handout.
3. Address stress and sleep with her PCP.
4. No endoscopic evaluation needed at this time. Return as needed.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her kitchen after school.

Anxiety: better. She dropped one of the extra committees and has kept the evening routine. Asleep by 10:30 most nights, still the odd early waking. GAD-7 5 today (9 in January). Does not want counseling or medicine.

IBS: fewer flares since cutting back on some trigger foods and adding fiber. Uses the PEG a few times a month. No bleeding, weight stable by her home scale.

Assessment: situational anxiety improving; IBS-M controlled.
Plan: continue current approach. Physical in August.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt cancelled 8/20 physical, pulled into building meetings before classes start. First opening that works with her schedule is the Friday school breaks for the holidays; booked 12/19 at 10:00. Flu/COVID to be done separately in October.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2025-26 flu vaccine L deltoid and 2025-26 COVID vaccine R deltoid. No acute illness, temp normal. Fine after 15 minutes of observation. Reminded her of the December physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, moved from August. First day of break and she sounds relieved.

Interval: IBS quiet most weeks; PEG maybe twice a month. Gut flares still track with busy stretches. Stress much more manageable this fall, sleeping through most nights. No new symptoms. NKDA. Only PEG as needed.

GAD-7 4, PHQ-9 3.

Exam: Vitals and weight as charted, unchanged. HEENT clear. Neck supple, no cervical adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. No edema. Calm, good eye contact.

A/P:
- Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids today. Mammogram order for January. FIT is due again; new kit given. Pap/HPV due next year, will do at next physical. Vaccines current for the season.
- IBS, mixed: stable on PEG as needed.
- Situational anxiety: much improved, no treatment needed.
Next physical in about a year; reach me by message for anything sooner.

documents.title: Results From Your Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count, chemistry and cholesterol all look good. Enjoy the break. Don't forget the stool kit when you get a chance.
